newsitem.title: FRANCE: Europe's airport seek to keep duty-free sales.
newsitem.headline: Europe's airport seek to keep duty-free sales.

text.p: Europe's airports are pressing for an extension of duty-free shopping within the EU and the dropping of the planned cut-off date of June 30,1999, Copenhagen airport's chief executive, Niels Boserup, told a press conference.
"Brussels should think twice before doing such a thing for the sake of principle. Why remove from the passenger a benefit which reduces the price he pays (for travel)?" he said.

"When it was decided to abolish duty-free goods within the EU, it was also the idea that there should be a common value added tax (VAT) level or something close to that, yet it varies widely within the EU," Boserup added.
It was also intended there should be at least harmonised excise taxes on luxury goods, alcohol and tobacco; something else which does not exist at present, he said.
However it will be difficult to rollback the abolition as it will require the unanimous agreement of all 15 EU Finance Ministers to change the plans now underway, he added.

Charter operators -- who tend to rely heavily on duty-free sales -- will be badly hit and some smaller airports "may find it difficult to finance infrastructure developments" if they lose this revenue, Boserup said.
